messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] DMRs from Tiling window and "diffMethPerChr"
parts:
rows shouldn't have NaNs unless there was sth went wrong in the previous steps. 
You can subset the methylDiff object with [] notation like you would subset a data frame, but I suggest doing this only if you understand what went wrong in the previous steps.

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] DMRs from Tiling window and "diffMethPerChr"
parts:
Thanks Altuna,

I can imagine how frustrating it can be for you to diagnose a problem when users' questions are not clear enough. Providing a "reproducable" code, however, can  be tricky. With my little knowledge of R I have been spending sleepless nights to diagnose the problem as well. My post below might not be "reproducable" but I believe it might give you some clue on the cause of the problem. This is the codes I run:

myobj.3 =read( file.list.3, pipeline=list(fraction=TRUE, chr.col=1, start.col=2, end.col=2, coverage.col=6, strand.col=3, freqC.col=5 ),
               sample.id=list("Neo-intimal SMC", "BMMC", "PBMC"), assembly="rn5", treatment=c(1,0, 0), context="CpG")

# get tiling window
tiles.3=tileMethylCounts(myobj.3, win.size=1000,step.size=1000)
meth.3.tile=unite(tiles.3, destrand=TRUE)
# calculate differential methylation from tile window 
myDiff.3=calculateDiffMeth(meth.3.tile, num.cores=2)
myDiff25p.3=get.methylDiff(myDiff.3, difference=25, qvalue=0.01)
get.res <- diffMethPerChr(myDiff.3, plot=FALSE, qvalue.cutoff = 0.01, meth.cutoff = 25) 

The interesting thing I find is that the "chr" set in myDiff25p.3 and get.res are not necessarily the same. I have exported them into a csv files below for your perusal:

myDiff25p.3
https://www.dropbox.com/s/m77tg0owkpo4jag/test-diff-meth-25p.txt?dl=0

and

get.res(i.e., diffMethPerChr)
https://www.dropbox.com/s/lhs28lowa317yep/test-diff-meth-per-chr.txt?dl=0

I wonder where the "chr*random" are coming from. Are the methods using different versions of the reference genome(i.e., rn5)?

Thanks a lot for your patience.

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] DMRs from Tiling window and "diffMethPerChr"
parts:
still not good enough, I'm afraid :/, it requires a lot of work on my part to read csv files and convert them to methylKit objects, I'm doing this on my spare time and have a really busy schedule. The less work it requires, the quicker I can help. Ideally what I mean by a reproducible example is that you should save the subset of the methylKit objects  in rdata format with saveRDS(), and send along the code that reads that file, runs the commands and reproduces the problem.

But I think your problems seems to be the * _random chromosomes. I can't tell at what point they enter your analysis, but I think you can ignore them, as it seems they don't have any differential methylation. Just subset your methylBase or methylDiff object with pattern matching using grep, sth like the following might work

meth.3.tile[grep("_random|chrUn",meth.3.tile$chr,invert=TRUE),]

In your case I would also suggest the following: you can try to pool your samples, you have no replicates for one of the conditions, pooling will enable you to compare conditions when there is no replicate for one of them and make sure you use the appropriate coverage thresholds, even though you can didn't get an error before it doesn't mean your results are reliable with 1X coverage.
http://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/methylKit/functions/pool-methods


tiles.3=tileMethylCounts(myobj.3, win.size=1000,step.size=1000)
meth.3.tile=unite(tiles.3, destrand=TRUE)
meth.3.tile=pool(meth.3.tile,sample.ids=c("test","control") )

myDiff.3=calculateDiffMeth(meth.3.tile, num.cores=2)
myDiff25p.3=get.methylDiff(myDiff.3, difference=25, qvalue=0.01)
get.res <- diffMethPerChr(myDiff.3, plot=FALSE, qvalue.cutoff = 0.01, meth.cutoff = 25)
